author: EmuCore - Hub
title: How GTA San Andreas Pushed the PS2 Beyond Its Limits
summary: MKTS uses Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas to discuss how a large PS2 world depended on memory budgeting, streaming and rendering choices.
searchKeywords: How GTA San Andreas Pushed the PS2 Beyond Its Limits

blocks.text: San Andreas is a useful case for studying a large world on hardware with tight memory. The video presents memory management, rendering and system constraints as connected design problems: the game cannot hold its entire world in fast memory, so it must select what to stream and draw as the player moves. This framing helps explain why a port or emulator can show a correct static image yet stumble during transitions, camera movement or traffic-heavy scenes.

The description labels the piece an architecture and software-engineering breakdown, but short summaries of complex game engines can simplify details that are not publicly documented. Treat the video as an interpretation of visible behavior and known PS2 constraints rather than a source of exact internal algorithms. When testing emulation, use repeatable routes through the city and record loading hitches, object pop-in and frame pacing separately. Those observations are more informative than a single peak frame-rate number.
